name: God Bullies
label: AmRep
lede: Mike Corso and Mike Hard started God Bullies in a Kalamazoo basement in 1986. Three years later they were making records for Amphetamine Reptile, and in 2024 the survivors finished an album for two bandmates who didn't get to hear it.

eras.title: A basement in Kalamazoo
eras.text: Corso reconnected with Hard, who had been singing in a Kalamazoo band called Debauched, and the band started in Corso's basement. Kalamazoo was big enough to make trouble in and small enough that everybody knew everybody.

years.big: "Mere words can not describe how incredibly horrid this band is"
years.src: Mike Corso interview · Wikipedia: God Bullies
years.h: God Bullies start in Mike Corso's basement
years.p: [[Mike Hard|e61fa499-27e7-423e-9835-fe1d374ad796]] on vocals, Corso on bass and Adam Berg on drums start the band in Kalamazoo, Michigan. Corso says Christian groups picketed over the name.
years.xp: Corso told winterviewz the band grew out of his basement after he reconnected with Hard. The line on the poster came from a write-up of the band, and the band blew the article up and used it for their next poster: "Mere words can not describe how incredibly horrid this band is."

years.h: "All I Want Is My Mamma" comes out on Mad Queen Records
years.p: The band's debut 7-inch is a 1988 release. A full set filmed at the Wayside in Kalamazoo that year shows the band at home before AmRep.
years.xp: The same year the band also put out "Fear and Pain" on Amphetamine Reptile, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Cabaret Metro, Chicago, April 20: four songs end up on vinyl
years.p: The April 20, 1988 Metro show becomes side two of Plastic Eye Miracle, next to five studio songs.

eras.title: The AmRep zoo takes them in
eras.text: Tom Hazelmyer's Amphetamine Reptile Records was collecting the loudest oddballs in the country, and God Bullies fit. Corso later said "I don't think there could have been a better label for GB's than AmRep," because it "always gave us total control." Three records in three years, recorded at Death Jam in Detroit.

years.h: Mad Queen issues Plastic Eye Miracle, AmRep reissues it in 1990
years.p: Hazelmyer did the cover art. Guitarist David B. Livingstone produced and engineered the record, half studio and half live.

years.cap: Mama Womb Womb, God Bullies' first AmRep LP (1989).
years.src: Wikipedia: Mama Womb Womb · Trouser Press · Echoes and Dust
years.h: Mama Womb Womb puts Georg Büchner on the first AmRep LP
years.p: Eleven songs in about 40 minutes, with a Büchner text set to music on "Red Blood". Livingstone plays guitar and keys, and engineers and mixes it himself.
years.xp:
The record is Hard, Livingstone, Corso and Berg, with Sue Moulds on backing vocals. Trouser Press points to it for Livingstone's harsher, colder guitar tone, before he got grungier on the follow-up.

Echoes and Dust describes the debut as recorded in lo-fi basement conditions on an 8-track.

years.cap: Mike Hard leaning into the crowd at the Venue, London, 1990
years.p: AmRep puts the God Bullies on a double 7-inch, with sermon and gospel samples running through it.
The third LP is cut at Death Jam Studios in Detroit: 11 songs, about 35 minutes. Peter Houpt plays slide on "Abigail" and Michael Cergizan plays guitar on "I Am Invisible".

eras.title: Drummers and bassists come and go
eras.text: Berg and Corso stepped back and the lineup turned over. The band kept putting out records on AmRep, then on other punk labels, and finished with a 1994 record for Jello Biafra's Alternative Tentacles.

years.cap: War on Everybody, God Bullies' last AmRep LP (1991).
years.src: Wikipedia: War on Everybody · Trouser Press
yt: Live at DC Space, Washington, Feb 12, 1991
years.h: Cows drummer Tony Oliveri joins for War on Everybody
years.p: Eric Polcyn plays bass. Berg and Corso only guest on the short "Senojmot". The record is cut in summer and fall 1991 at Death Jam in Detroit.
years.xp:
Hard, Livingstone, Oliveri and Polcyn are the core of the record. Bruce White sings on the opening track. At 12 songs and about 38 minutes, it is the last God Bullies LP AmRep released.

Two live sets from the year are on video, one from DC Space in Washington on February 12 and one from July 11.

years.src: Mike Corso interview · Echoes and Dust
years.h: Jello Biafra wants a God Bullies record, to point people at Thrall
years.p: Corso, who says he was kicked out after the first three LPs, is back on bass for Kill the King. Hard says Biafra suggested a God Bullies record to draw attention to [[Thrall|94d6bbba-8ec4-4834-ab9b-0f4c49c73315]], his new project.
years.xp:
Hard says Biafra's idea was a God Bullies album that would send people toward Thrall, the Detroit band Hard was starting. He reunited the original members to make it.

Echoes and Dust quotes Hard saying it was the first time the band used an actual recording studio: Alternative Tentacles asked for the record while God Bullies were inactive.

years.h: A "Millennium" 7-inch on Radial Records, then quiet
years.p: The single is the last release before the band goes silent. Hard also turns up on screen with Ron Asheton in the 1995 film Mosquito.

eras.title: The AmRep 25th reunion
eras.text: Amphetamine Reptile turned 25 and got its bands back on stage. God Bullies were among the ones people kept talking about afterwards.

years.cap: God Bullies live at Grumpy's Downtown, Minneapolis, August 28, 2010
yt: Shakin' All Over with Shannon Selberg, AmRep 25th anniversary
years.h: God Bullies play AmRep's 25th anniversary, then tour as "War On Peace"
years.p: [[Mike Hard|e61fa499-27e7-423e-9835-fe1d374ad796]], David B. Livingstone, Mike Corso, Adam Berg and guitarist Johnnie Johnson are the lineup.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says sets ran 25 to 30 songs a night. Yourfleshmag wrote that God Bullies were easily one of the three bands generating the most discussion at the anniversary event.

At the anniversary show they covered "Shakin' All Over" with Shannon Selberg of Cows.

eras.title: Two friends gone, one record made
eras.text: Hard, Livingstone and Johnnie Johnson were working together in a new band when both men died. The surviving members finished the God Bullies album they had started.

years.h: David B. Livingstone dies in February
years.p: The guitarist who engineered and mixed the AmRep-era records dies in 2023, while working with Hard and Johnnie Johnson III on Pig Harvest, a project co-founded in November 2021. No cause is given in the sources.

q: We wanted to honor them both.
years.src: Echoes and Dust · Louder Than War · Wikipedia
years.h: Doing it for both of them
years.p: Mike Hard, Kodrik, O'Harris and Carinci reform God Bullies to finish the record, with Livingstone's co-writing on it.
years.xp: Hard says Johnnie Johnson started the reunion by asking founding members to play a 25th anniversary show for Thrall. After Johnson's sudden death, the surviving members decided to complete the album for both him and Livingstone. Hard says the new lineup is largely Thrall, the Detroit band he has played with for 32 years.

years.src: Wikipedia · No Echo · Louder Than War · Echoes and Dust
years.p: Recorded at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio in Chicago with producer Sanford Parker, out October 4, 2024 on Reptilian Records. The vinyl run is 750 copies.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the sessions were in April 2024, shortly before [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s death. Hard and Kodrik say Parker pushed for a live sound with few overdubs, and the band toured the Midwest from October.

Echoes and Dust says it was recorded in two days.

Louder Than War: As Above So Below
